title: What Commons Production Networks Is
definition: Commons Production Networks: networks producing shared goods.
description:
Strip Commons Production Networks to its essence and you get networks producing shared goods. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Post-Scarcity Economy: first commons licenses understanding, then network logistics prototypes, then contribution tracking operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of network hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Commons Production Networks
title: Real Research Today: Commons Production Networks
definition: Today's documented research behind Commons Production Networks.
description:
The road to Commons Production Networks is already being paved. Open-source hardware (Arduino, RISC-V) shows zero-marginal-cost production at scale. The Doughnut Economics model (Kate Raworth, Amsterdam) reframes growth within planetary bounds.

Elinor Ostrom's Nobel-winning work on governing the commons underpins commons economics. Together these programs form the commons licenses foundation that Commons Production Networks will build on — the network logistics results, the contribution tracking methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as network logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — First city-scale network hulls pilots launch: commons licenses i
title: 2030 — First city-scale network hulls pilots launch: commons licenses i
definition: 2030 milestone on the Commons Production Networks roadmap.
description:
First city-scale network hulls pilots launch: commons licenses issuance and network logistics exchange running live.

What must be true first: the commons licenses results have to replicate outside the lab, network logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and contribution tracking operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed commons licenses demonstrations, network logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting contribution tracking uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Commons Production Networks
definition: Estimates Commons Production Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Commons Production Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Commons Production Networks Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Commons Production Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Commons Production Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 65057 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where commons licenses monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or contribution tracking maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Commons Production Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Commons Production Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Commons Production Networks — networks producing shared goods.

Phase 1 — Prove (commons licenses): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (contribution tracking): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (governance): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and open source-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
